drone: unspecified small X-frame quadrotor with 3-blade props (SPCUP19 team AGH), fixed on a stand in an anechoic chamber; 8-ch electret cube array below it + AKG C451 B reference mic on a separate stand
frame: AGH.yaml frame: origin = centroid of the 8 array mics (derived); x, y parallel to the loudspeaker axes of 'static clean/info.xlsx' (azimuth counter-clockwise from +x); z up, towards the drone; metres. The drone's own heading relative to x, y is not documented.

channel_map.text: row i = wav channel i of 'ego-noise/mic array/*.wav' (each channel's position was fitted from that channel's own TDOAs)

array8.rotor_pos_null_reason: No rotor coordinates are documented. AGH.yaml: SRP-PHAT / MUSIC on the ego-noise files puts the rotor noise at elevation ~58-62 deg above the array centre, but azimuth peaks (~68, 126, -132, -48 deg) have only 1-1.5 dB contrast and range is unresolved. This campaign's attempt (ego-noise/mic array/4.wav, setting 20, the four BPF lines 209.6/214.3/216.0/217.4 Hz -> shaft rates 69.85/71.47/72.02/72.49 Hz refined by comb search; per-rotor harmonic families k <= 70, f <= 5 kHz, rank-1 cross-spectral vectors, phase-only near-field beam on a 3-D grid +-0.3 m x +-0.3 m x -0.1..0.4 m) failed: beam peaks 0.18-0.21 against a grid median 0.12-0.13, two of four peaks on the grid edge, the other two at implausible places (z ~ 0). The rotor field at this array is not explained by four point sources with the derived mic_pos.

rotor_plane_height_above_array_centre_m.source: report Fig. 2 photo (pdfimages img-001): prop plane ~255 px above the mid-point between the two mic layers, layer gap 0.101 m ~150-160 px at that depth; perspective not corrected

rotor_radius_from_axis_m.source: height 0.16 m and SRP elevation 58-62 deg (AGH.yaml) -> 0.085-0.10 m; Fig. 2 shows a small racing X-frame (motor spacing consistent with ~0.2 m diagonal)

rotor_azimuths.source: SRP azimuth peaks ~68/126/-132/-48 deg have 1-1.5 dB contrast (AGH.yaml); not usable

mic_pos.basis: AGH.yaml: regular-model vs unconstrained fit differ 0.3/0.9/2.3 cm (x/y/z); layer gap 0.101 m is uncertain by ~+-0.03 m; scale +-1 % with c

array8.notes: Two horizontal 4-mic squares (radius 0.116 m, 0.101 m apart): lower layer = channels 0, 2, 4, 6; upper = 1, 3, 5, 7. The drone sits on posts above the upper plate. All four rotors run in every array take; at setting 20 they are separable by speed (4 distinct BPF lines), at higher settings they overlap more.

channel_map.text: single channel (AKG C451 B reference condenser mic)

sources: report Fig. 2 (mic on its own stand beside the drone)
ref_mic.notes: No coordinates anywhere; only visible in Fig. 2 (beside the drone, roughly at arm / upper-array height, a few dm from the nearest rotor). At the common setting 160 the single-rotor RMS is rotor 4 -20.8, rotor 1 -22.7, rotor 3 -24.8, rotor 2 -29.3 dBFS (AGH.yaml) - a level ordering, not a geometry. One mic only, so the single-rotor takes cannot test spreading across microphones.

open_questions: Rotor positions (and which physical rotor is the team's 'rotor 1..4') are undocumented; only elevation (~58-62 deg) is constrained acoustically, height/radius only roughly from the photo. Asking the AGH team or fitting rotor positions as free parameters in the spreading test are the remaining routes.
Reference-mic position unknown (single-rotor takes therefore carry no geometry).
Array layer gap (0.101 m) is the least certain mic coordinate (+-0.03 m).
